name: Lemon balm

schedule.notes: Cut hard before flowering — leaves get bitter after. Two flushes per season.

harvest.cues: Stems 6+ in, leaves bright green and lemon-scented. Cut whole stems 2 in above the soil.
harvest.storageNotes: Best fresh. Dries OK but loses much aroma. Freeze chopped in water cubes for tea.

varieties.name: Common Lemon Balm
varieties.notes: Bright green, classic lemony mint scent.

varieties.name: Aurea (Golden)
varieties.notes: Yellow-variegated leaves. Slightly less vigorous, slightly less lemony.

notes: Self-seeds aggressively — let some flower for bees, but cut the rest hard to limit volunteers. Tea favorite; rub a leaf on the back of your wrist for natural perfume.
